title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one need-exception governs one intervention at 35 and two at 65
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. The newly completed Sloane2435 age chapter distinguishes bloodletting from medicinal purging: after35, avoid the former unless great need and prefer the latter; after65, avoid both unless great need. Explore a repeated construction over the complete existing f85r2 S/W blocks with stable intervention roles and changed exception scope. This is a new conditional content candidate, not a continuation of the old faculty dictionary or a four-figures/four-thresholds identification.

design.mechanism: A repeated conditional prohibition takes an intervention set; the later condition enlarges that set from one intervention to both while retaining the same great-need exception.
design.unit: Entire already acquired f85r2 S.12–17 and W.18–23, both possible source-condition orientations retained. Full N/E and outside text remain context, not suppressed counterevidence. No new target access.
design.contrast: One stable scope-taking rule over two distinct intervention roles versus an undifferentiated old-person treatment ban or four independent age names.
design.prediction: The younger condition permits/preferentially recommends purging without requiring the exceptional need that licenses bloodletting; the older condition puts BOTH interventions under the exception. Swapping the two intervention identities globally does not remove the one-member versus two-member scope difference, and a universal treatment-ban model gets the younger purging permission wrong.
actual_referents: BL Sloane2435, dated1265–1270, North France, complete chapter20 f31r–32v top, acquired in I. Working semantic reading sections8 and12 owns35 and65 respectively; the provisional45 was expressly corrected.

GDT1042 complete spatial-block census gives S26 groups and W36/35/37 groups in ZL/IT/RF. S/W share six ZL whole types: aiin, ain, chedy, or, qodaiin, shedy. Reader differences are retained; this set is navigation/capacity, not six translated words.

The measured structural baseline allows reusable directed constructions but identifies no exception marker, intervention name, numeral or patient. Historical usage is medical conduct directed toward a person, not the pictured figure necessarily performing treatment.
design.additional_assumption: Conditionally, two whole spatial blocks contain versions of one intervention rule. Only their common construction is hypothesized; their physical orientation is not read as chronological order, and35/65 are not asserted as written target numbers. A finite candidate must distinguish two intervention roles, need and prohibition, and explicitly realize their scope.

finite_content_core.case_A: AFTER35(patient): prohibit BLOODLETTING unless GREAT_NEED; prefer PURGING to BLOODLETTING.
finite_content_core.case_B: AFTER65(patient): prohibit BLOODLETTING and PURGING unless GREAT_NEED.
finite_content_core.role_budget: At most four new hypothesized reusable core values: BLOODLETTING, PURGING, GREAT_NEED and PROHIBITION. Condition and comparison structure must be authored as explicit constructions before fitting. Age values may remain parameters, but their guard cannot disappear.
finite_content_core.unresolved_groups: All target groups are currently semantically unassigned under this candidate. Four proposed role values are NOT four identified words. The remaining source chapter includes diet, exercise, sexuality, preparations and care; none is silently claimed translated by this small core. A full block reading must account for all groups and any additional propositions it selects.
finite_content_core.no_free_repairs: Do not import GDT1045/1046's aiin RecipientRef, qod attraction, ar nominalizer or HOT/COLD dictionaries. Do not choose a different sense of the same intervention between cases, add unmarked negation, or treat permission as an actual performed event.

design.strongest_known_countercase: GDT1042 has no common exact first group for four age headings, aiin is the only whole shared by all four blocks, and its or-aiin bigram is not stable in IT. GDT1045 only supplies conditional qod type coverage, not an independently bound W sentence; GDT1046's strict NOM extension fails IT/RF ar-ar. None establishes a medical construction here. Source35 lies inside the second broad age, so equating the four broad ages to treatment thresholds is specifically wrong.
design.smallest_next_test: One bounded construction-authoring pass on the two complete saved blocks: freeze the two source cores and both orientations, nominate at most four core-role whole types with their exact reader realizations, then write the same scope rule twice and inspect every occurrence of its chosen operators on this already owned page. List every residual group without filling it. If no written scope difference separates one intervention from both, classify this candidate as missing binding; if a fixed proposal conflicts with an occurrence, retain that countercase. No decoder, corpus census or reserve is needed.
design.new_input_vs_predecessors: The new input is the completed native Sloane chapter with corrected35 and the explicit one-action/two-action exception contrast. IDEA34/66/616 supply generic exception mechanisms; IDEA544 has Hippocratic treatment guards and IDEA759 a permission expiring after recovery. This card specifies a different reusable set-scope contrast and nominates a finite existing paired context. It does not reopen any failed faculty grammar.
design.source_layer: I is a complete provisional semantic reading with native ownership and1911 comparative collation, not a fully diplomatic transcription. No source image was reopened in K.
design.assessment: RAW only. No selected meaning, completed whole reading, experiment result, novelty proof or independent confirmation.
